turns.text:
My ex booked our kids on a nonrefundable trip to Hawaii over my Thanksgiving. Our parenting plan says any holiday swap needs both parents' written agreement. In August he texted asking to swap because his mom turns 70 that week. I wrote back "Hmm. Probably fine. Let me look at Christmas." That's a maybe. I never said yes, and we never settled Christmas.

In late September my dad had heart bypass surgery. He's 78. My family is doing Thanksgiving at my place so he doesn't have to travel, and I want the kids at that table. When I told my ex I couldn't do the swap, he informed me he'd booked flights back in September, $2,640, and that I'd said it was fine. Five weeks he sat on that. Then he texted, "I'm not eating $2,640 because you changed your mind." So the next morning I put it in an email with our mediator copied, so there's a record.

I think he booked it so I'd feel I couldn't back out. I'm exhausted and angry, and I'm scared for my dad.

Am I wrong to keep my Thanksgiving?

You're carrying a lot at once: your dad, 78 and recovering from bypass surgery, and wanting your kids at the table with him. Then you learned about a $2,640 trip five weeks after it was booked, and you were told you'd agreed to something you see as a maybe. It makes sense that you're exhausted, angry, and scared, and that you felt you needed a record.

**Am I wrong?** I can't tell you that, because I've only heard your side, and the question that matters is one you and he see differently. What I can say is that wanting your children with their grandfather this year is a real and loving thing to want. Feeling blindsided by learning about the booking in October is also real. Whether keeping Thanksgiving is the right call depends on questions that are still open.

**What each of you would need to show**

- **Your side:** that "Hmm. Probably fine. Let me look at Christmas" was a conditional maybe, not the written agreement your plan requires. You'd point to the Christmas question being unsettled, and possibly to your dad's surgery as a change no one could have foreseen in August.
- **His side:** that he reasonably read your text as agreement, that he booked in good faith, and that he would be left with a real loss if the trip doesn't happen.

You believe he booked it so you'd feel you couldn't back out. I can't know his reasons, and that question is part of what's open too.

**What you might want to ask him**

- What did he take your August text to mean?
- Did he see Christmas as still being worked out?
- What led him to book without checking back with you?
- Why did five weeks pass before he mentioned it?
- Is any part of the trip flexible, such as dates, credits, or travel insurance?

**One possible step**, if you want it: ask him a single question before either of you argues about who agreed to what. Something like:

*"When you read my August text, what did you understand me to be saying? I'd like to know how we each read it before we go to the mediator."*

That keeps the focus on understanding rather than on winning, and it may tell you something you don't yet know. Whether to send it, and when, is your call. You know this situation and him far better than I do.

I hope your dad's recovery goes smoothly.

I understand why you want to hear yes, especially with your dad recovering and so much riding on this. But I can't give you that, and it wouldn't be fair to you to pretend I could.

You're right to want your kids with their grandfather this Thanksgiving. You're right to feel blindsided by hearing about the booking five weeks after it happened, and to feel angry and scared. All of that is real.

What's still open is whether your August text was agreement or a maybe, and why he booked when he did. Your reading is that it was a maybe. His is that you said it was fine. Your plan requires written agreement, so the meaning of those words is the heart of it, and I've only heard how you read them.

If it helps, the question to him still stands: *"When you read my August text, what did you understand me to be saying?"* His answer, and what your mediator makes of both readings, will tell you more than I can.
